requirements_summary: Workloads: real-time chat for traders (sub-second decisioning), embeddings for fast similarity search, reranking for alert prioritization.
Throughput: sustained 120-150 RPS during market-open windows; burst to 300 RPS for ~3-7 minute intervals.
Latency SLOs: p95 first-token <= 250ms for short prompts; end-to-end p95 <= 600ms for ~512-token outputs. p99 targets negotiable but requested for core routes.
Availability: target 99.95% overall, customer pushing 99.99% during market hours; negotiating financial credits for misses.
Reserved capacity ask: initial recommendation 8 GPUs (H100 equiv) with 2 warm spares for maintenance/failover; request Redwood sizing by model mix following POC.
SLA asks: latency SLOs with credit model, explicit RTO for cross-region failover (3-5m), remediation windows and incident runbook commitments.
Security: VPC-only deployment, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logs retention 12+ months, US-only data residency.
Fallback & routing: require model-variant fallback chain + cross-region active-passive failover; no external burst to Redwood hosted shared pool.
Observability: per-route p50/p95/p99 metrics, token-level latency/cost breakdown, tracing hooks and alerting integrated into customer pager system.
notes:
CRM notes: Focused on Dedicated capacity evaluation and reliability/fallback design.
- Customer uses LLMs in trader workflows; outages during market-open are high-risk (P&L impact).
- Primary asks: deterministic throughput guarantees, clear latency SLOs, reserved GPU planning with warm spares, and an explicit fallback strategy that preserves privacy.
- Reliability design discussed: cross-region active-passive failover (us-east-1 -> us-west-2), expected RTO 3-5 minutes, async KV/prefix cache replication with eventual consistency window defined in runbook.
- Model-variant fallback chain proposed: primary FP32 model -> quantized 8-bit variant (same arch) -> smaller faster model (e.g., Llama-2-chat-medium) -> deny or return degraded-but-safe response (no spill to shared hosted pool). Customer requires policy config by route and audit trail of fallback events.
- Cache strategy: session stickiness to regional instance to reduce cold starts; pre-warm caches before market-open using scheduled prefetch job.
- Capacity spillover: explicitly disallowed to Redwood hosted/shared pool for trade data; customer may allow private bursting to a second Dedicated region under contract.
- POC deliverables: observed per-GPU throughput, p95/p99 latency distributions, failover runbook test results, recommended reserved GPU count and buffer.
- Blockers: final SLA language around latency credits, legal approval for data residency addendum, network peering maintenance window.
- Quotes: CTO: "We need predictable behavior at 09:30 ET. Any black swan downtime is unacceptable."
